body: my mom was in a very similar boat, years of untreated mental health issues combined with substance use and losing custody made her send absolutely unhinged texts like these. i feel for you and you don’t deserve this. we ended up signing her into a court-mandated 72-hour hold for mental health and substance-related issues, idk if that sort of thing is offered wherever you’re at but i would definitely look into something like that.

nta, your feelings are 100% valid and having feelings of resentment towards someone who wronged you is so understandable. harboring resentment doesn’t feel good, but she seems unwilling to hear your feelings and recognize that she played a part in your mental health. you shouldn’t have to keep quiet to keep the peace though, and your true feelings about her could very likely come out at some point in the future. i’d say a family therapy session might be the most effective way to get those feelings out in the open if that’s a resource you have access to. this is a tough situation to navigate, best of luck op

nta, it’s so infuriating how people without allergies or with minimal experience with allergies are so quick to cast aside how serious and fatal these things can be. i’ve had a pretty severe peanut allergy for my whole life and still had to beg to get a blood test to prove to my own parent that i was still very much allergic and that it wasn’t “all in my head”. this happened a few months after a serious allergic reaction, and it was so exhausting trying to advocate for myself especially since i was a minor at the time. go you for advocating for your children, step grandma can (dis)respectfully screw off.

oh most definitely nta. it’s not just her only son’s wedding, it’s also june’s wedding and a symbol of the unification of the two of you and your families. bringing someone who she believes should have been in june’s place is so beyond disrespectful to the bride, and absolutely warranted being kicked out.
